scope.period: from the Companions and early generations through contemporary scholars
scope.goal: Maintain a continuously extensible Sunni-oriented scholarly corpus without treating the label alone as sufficient evidence.

importantTerminology.projectProfile: The requested primary corpus is Athari/Salafi-oriented Sunni scholarship plus the four Sunni schools of jurisprudence.
importantTerminology.classificationNote: The term Ahl al-Sunnah has historically been used differently by Sunni authorities; the project must not present a sectarian classification as an uncontested universal fact.

primary: Athari/Salafi creed and its scholarly works
recognized Sunni jurists of Hanafi, Maliki, Shafi'i and Hanbali schools
classical and contemporary Sunni scholarship whose methodology matches the project's stated corpus policy

authors.verification: Do not classify an author solely by a website tag; use bibliographic records and authoritative biographical sources.

defaultCorpus: explicitly sectarian works outside the project's stated Sunni corpus
exclusion.comparativeResearch: If comparative material is ever added, it must live in a separate clearly labelled research corpus and must never be presented as part of the primary Sunni corpus.

workflow: discover new books from approved sources
index searchable metadata and permitted text
record source URL and retrieval date
never: auto-copy copyrighted full books without permission

downloadPolicy.rule: Only expose direct downloads when the source or rights holder permits redistribution; otherwise provide a source link and bibliographic metadata.
